verdict_reason: Only 7 of the pile's 16 photos are on the sheet, and every one of them belongs to the single small complex at the north-east corner of Hoan Kiem Lake: the Thap But stone tower on its rockery, the Dac Nguyet Lau gate, and The Huc Bridge to Ngoc Son temple. The gate plaque was read directly - the red name-board says '得月樓' (Dac Nguyet Lau) with the flanking couplet '不厭湖上月 / 宛在水中央' - which is the gate at the foot of The Huc Bridge, so this is a named place, not an arbitrary pin. Four tiles are the bridge itself (one by day, three as red-lit night long exposures with reflections). Nothing on the sheet is anywhere else. Caveats: with 7 of 16 tiles visible I cannot rule out that the missing 9 wander, and the ids form only three or four blocks (11526..., 3736..., 6113..., 6999...), so the agreement is between a handful of contributors.

photos.evidence: A tall tapered tower of stacked rough stone blocks rising from an artificial rockery, carrying large red-painted Chinese characters on its shaft - the character '天' is clear, consistent with the well-known three-character inscription 'Ta Thanh Thien' on Thap But (the Pen Tower). A small stone shrine with vertical character panels and a glass offering case sits in the rocks at its foot; a child stands on the rock steps.

Cropped and upscaled 2.5x: a masonry gate-tower with an upswept tiled roof, dragon ridge finials, a pale blue tympanum painted with two phoenixes around a large circular opening, and a red name-board reading '得月樓' (Dac Nguyet Lau, 'moon-catching tower'), flanked by the couplet '不厭湖上月' and '宛在水中央'. This is the gate at the entrance to The Huc Bridge / Ngoc Son temple on Hoan Kiem Lake.

Cropped and upscaled 3x: the same rockery as 11526176614, with the stone tower's red character panels above and, at right, a small stone shrine built into the rocks whose incised couplets include '新祠香火福...' and '...湖山...' (lake-and-mountain wording). Same child, same rock steps - the Thap But mound at the Ngoc Son entrance.
Looking along a plank deck between scarlet timber balustrades with square red newel posts, dense green trees closing over the far end and people sitting on the deck - the walkway of The Huc Bridge.
Night long exposure: an arched bridge outlined in red light with its full reflection in still black water, dark foliage overhead - the illuminated The Huc Bridge on Hoan Kiem Lake.
Night long exposure of the same red-lit arched bridge with green point-lights among the trees on the bank and the bridge mirrored in the lake.
Another night exposure of the same subject from slightly further left; the red-outlined arch, its regular pile bays and the reflection are identical to 6999453125.
